problem.aria: Problem diagram: weather, time, events and traffic push the demand of a zone; in Downtown, on a Friday at 18:00, there are 165 requests and only 110 drivers, and that gap causes long waits and cancellations, or idle drivers if it happens the other way round.
problem.zoneSub: requests and possible trips in 15 min
problem.outANote:
Long waits, more cancellations
and less satisfied users
problem.outBNote:
Fewer trips per driver,
less income and log-offs
problem.outBTag: In another zone or at another time
problem.challenge: Challenge: balance supply and demand within minutes, zone by zone

ts.aria: Chart: weighted average of the last four Fridays (133), adjusted for rain (157) and for live demand (165).

km.aria: Three scatter plots of nine zones with k-means: badly placed initial centres, centres moved to the mean of each group and convergence into three groups.
km.c1:
Two centres land in the same
business zone. Each zone joins
its nearest centre.
km.c2:
Each centre moves to the mean
of its zones. A and C change
group.
km.c3:
No zone changes: 3 groups
remain. Centre (C) is a
business zone.

reg.aria: Chart: demand falls as the price multiplier rises and driver supply goes up; they cross at 1.39×, with about 136 trips.

loop.aria: Chart: the multiplier rises from 1.00 to 1.40 in five minutes, settles near 1.4 and returns to 1.00 when demand drops; below, the demand/supply ratio.
